analysis:
Reviewed unit 0 and independently checked the replayed patches, file metadata and supplied source. changelog.d/installer-release-file-modes.md:3 and docs/operations/provider-release.md:411–414 describe release extraction using /usr/bin/tar under umask 022 while retaining separate private-state modes. The documentation date also changes; both files have mode 100644. No executable installer implementation is supplied, so the documentation establishes neither a permission regression nor successful enforcement. Broader readability of public release artifacts does not itself expose prompts, process keys or provider tokens (A-001, A-003, A-008), and umask 022 does not itself grant other users write access.
The release documentation retains the production Apple-team signature requirement and distinguishes device-attestation trust from code identity. Supplied surrounding text also separates official registration from serving authorization (BASE docs/operations/provider-release.md:477–479). No supported change to T-013/T-054 protections, TB-011 authorization, encryption, billing, cache storage or privileged-helper authority is evidenced.
The material unresolved integration question is the actual scripts/install.sh install_bundle_atomically implementation: verify that the umask override is limited to extraction, cannot broaden permissions on later credentials/private state, and preserves staged integrity checks. Inspect archive and resulting installation modes rather than relying on prose. This batch cannot resolve that contract: executable source is absent and replay explicitly omits two reviewed source units. These are coverage limits, not observed missing controls; no finding is supported.
